articles.title: Korea Ratings Resolves to Convene Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders to Appoint Jonathan Mark Cornish as Non-Executive Director - Digital Today
articles.summary:
[Digital Today AI Disclosure Team] Credit rating agency Korea Ratings (034950) announced on Sept. 11 that it has resolved to convene an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders and table an agenda for the new appointment of Jonathan Mark Cornish as a non-executive director. The extraordinary general meeting of shareholders will be held on Oct. 29, 2026, at 10 a.m. at Lounge K on the 7th floor of the Kyobo Securities Building, 97 Uisadang-daero, Yeongdeungpo-gu, Seoul.

The record date for voting rights is set for Sept. 30, 2026, and the date of the board resolution is recorded as Sept. 11, 2026. Three outside directors attended the board meeting. The sole agenda item for this extraordinary general meeting of shareholders is Proposal No.

1, which is the new appointment of Jonathan Mark Cornish as a non-executive director. Cornish was born in September 1968, and his term of office runs until the date of the annual general meeting of shareholders for the 2027 fiscal year. His current professional background specifies that he serves as Executive Director, Manager in Charge, and Responsible Officer at Fitch (Hong Kong), and is employed as Managing Director and Head of APAC Financial Institutions. According to Korea Ratings' consolidated financial status as of the December 2025 settlement of accounts, total assets stand at 187.5 billion won, total liabilities at 41.5 billion won, and total equity at 146 billion won. Revenue is 109.8 billion won, operating profit is 34.3 billion won, and net income is 29.4 billion won.

articles.title: Trump Claims 'Mental Victory' as Convention Declares 'Huge Success' Despite Empty Seats and Exiting Crowds - The Hankyoreh
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump has self-evaluated that a two-day convention held ahead of the November midterm elections was a "huge success" with sold-out crowds. However, even on the closing day of the 10th (local time), numerous sections of the upper level of the venue were empty, and audience members were captured leaving their seats during the speech. Box office results fell short of his claims, with US President Trump's viewership ratings for his first-day speech also coming in lower than usual for the same time slot. According to US media outlets including the New York Times (NYT) and the Associated Press (AP) on this day, US President Trump claimed during his closing speech at the convention held at the American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas, that the venue was "packed" and that there were "thousands of people" outside as well. He appealed to supporters by urging them to "vote as if I were on the ballot," setting out to rally midterm election sentiment. Vice President JD Vance also spoke prior to US President Trump, attacking the Democrats as "lunatics" and emphasizing traditional families, American manufacturing, and religious freedom. The Guardian reported that when Vance appeared, he received an enthusiastic welcome, with chants of "JD" and slogans demanding a run in the 2028 presidential election erupting.

However, interior footage of the venue released by local Dallas media outlet the Dallas Morning News confirmed multiple empty seats. The progressive online media outlet The Daily Beast also reported that the upper level and some VIP sections were empty, and that while US President Trump was giving his speech, audience members were leaving the venue and staff members had begun preparing for tear-down. It reported that the large-scale crowds claimed by US President Trump were not confirmed outside the venue either. This box office atmosphere, which failed to meet expectations, was already detected from the first day. US President Trump spoke for about 105 minutes on the 9th, but according to preliminary Nielsen figures, average viewership on Fox News, which broadcast the speech from 9 to 11 p.m., stood at 2.5 million, fewer than regular programs in the same time slot, the New York Times reported. The on-site audience stands were not completely filled either. When the convention began, the arena floor where state delegations were seated was mostly full, but only about half of the lower-level stands were filled, and the upper level was mostly empty, the Wall Street Journal reported.

Reuters reported that while US President Trump claimed the 21,000-seat arena was packed, a significant portion of the upper-level seats were empty during the speech. These scenes ran counter to US President Trump's own assessment. He wrote on Truth Social that day, "Last night's convention in Dallas was bigger and more important than anyone thought possible, achieving a sold-out, massive success." He also claimed that it recorded higher viewership ratings than a National Football League (NFL) game, and that thousands who failed to enter were outside the venue. US media outlets analyzed this convention as an election-purpose event aimed at highlighting the achievements of the second Trump administration and rallying the core base ahead of the midterm elections. Amid rising international oil prices and living costs stemming from the prolonged war in Iran, US President Trump's state approval ratings have also declined.

articles.title: President Lee's Approval Rating Dips into 30% Range for First Time... Negative Outweighs Positive Across All Age Groups
articles.summary:
President Lee's job approval rating stood at 38%, according to a public opinion poll released on the 11th by Gallup Korea, which was conducted from the 8th to the 10 among 1,000 adults aged 18 and older nationwide (conducted via phone interviews, with a 95% confidence level and a sampling error of ±3.1 percentage points; further details are available on the National Election Survey Deliberation Commission website). Negative assessments stood at 51%. In the previous week's survey, positive assessments were 40% and negative assessments were 51%.

President Lee's job approval rating had stood at 64% in the third week of May survey, which was the final poll before the June 3 local elections, but has fallen by 26 percentage points in about three months' time. Based on Gallup Korea surveys, the fastest drop in a former president's job approval rating below 40% was recorded by former President Yoon Suk Yeol at just two months into his term, followed by former President Park Geun-hye at 1 year and 10 months, and former President Moon Jae-in at 2 years and 5 months.

As for the reasons behind negative evaluations, real estate policy was the most frequent response at 24%, followed by personnel appointments at 16%, the economy and public livelihood at 11%, and moral issues and dodging his own trials at 6%. Responses citing personnel appointments as a reason for negative evaluation rose by 7 percentage points from the previous week. Foreign policy was the most common reason given for positive evaluations at 19%.

By age group, negative evaluations outnumbered positive evaluations across all age brackets, including those in their 40s and 50s, who are considered part of the traditional support base. Notably, positive evaluations among those in their 40s dropped by 10 percentage points from the previous week to 45%. Positive evaluations were lowest among those in their 20s and those aged 70 and older, both at 31%.

articles.title: Kim Min-seok’s ‘Seoul Mayor Candidate’ Notes and By-election Remarks Spark Backlash from Legal and Political Circles Amid Accusations of Pressuring Judiciary
articles.summary:
Democratic Party leader Kim Min-seok caused a stir in political and legal circles on the 10th by stating that next year's Seoul mayoral by-election has a 99.99% probability of taking place, drawing criticism that the ruling party leader effectively issued guidelines to the judiciary. Appearing on the YouTube channel "Democratic Party TV" that day, Kim said, "I believe there is a 99.99% chance that the Seoul mayoral election and the Gangneung National Assembly by-election will happen." When the host asked, "Next year?", Kim replied, "We bear responsibility for the general election as well as the Seoul and Gangneung by-elections, so it is only natural that we prepare for them." The controversy arose after press cameras captured Kim on his notebook in the National Assembly plenary chamber the previous day (the 9th), where he had written "Seoul Mayor Candidate" alongside the names of former Democratic Party leader Jeong Cheong-rae, Blue House Chief of Staff Kang Hoon-sik, and former National Assembly Speaker Woo Won-shik.

The opposition party pointed out that Kim was pressuring the judiciary to hand down a guilty verdict against Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon. People Power Party floor leader Jung Jeom-sik stated on Facebook that day, "By taking it as a fait accompli that next year's April Seoul mayoral by-election will be held, he is publicizing the narrative that 'Mayor Oh is guilty' and signaling pressure on the judiciary to deliver a guilty verdict. The government and the ruling party must stop their petty attempts to undermine opposition local government heads and pressure the judiciary." A lawyer who formerly served as a presiding judge told this newspaper, "Given that Mayor Oh's trial remains ongoing, wouldn't it be better for [Kim] to exercise some restraint and self-control?

If the ruling party leader publicly made such remarks with the intent to influence the judge, it is nothing short of inappropriate." Another lawyer with a background as a judge noted, "It is merely an expression of his personal thoughts, but politically inappropriate." A lawyer who previously served as a prosecutor also remarked, "I think it is an inappropriate comment because it can impose a certain level of psychological pressure on the judiciary. Isn't this a case where only the first trial has concluded? An acquittal could come out in the appellate court, so jumping to conclusions like that seems a bit excessive."

For next year's Seoul mayoral by-election to be held as the ruling party predicts, Mayor Oh must receive a final confirmation of a fine of 1 million won or more—a sentence that invalidates an election victory—from the Supreme Court (the third instance). Under the Public Official Election Act, for a by-election to be held in April of next year, the sentence must be finally confirmed by the end of February next year. The core issue is that this trial involves a case investigated and indicted by a special prosecutor.

Under the current Special Prosecutor Act, cases prosecuted by a special prosecutor must be handled with the highest priority over other trials, following the "6-3-3 rule," which mandates that the first trial be completed within six months, and the second and third trials within three months each from the date of the previous instance's sentencing. If the trials gain momentum according to the legal deadlines, there is a high possibility that a final conclusion by the Supreme Court will emerge before the end of February next year. If a guilty verdict at the level of an election-invalidating sentence is handed down by the third instance before the end of February, the Seoul mayoral by-election will be held on April 7 next year.

Conversely, if the appellate or supreme court procedures are delayed and the confirmation timing spills over past March next year, the next by-election is projected to take place on October 6 next year.

articles.title: Cheong Wa Dae says President Lee expressed intent not to seek consecutive term; PPP calls it a sign of desperation for a clever constitutional amendment
articles.summary:
Cheong Wa Dae explained that President Lee Jae-myung’s remark that "my term is clearly limited by the Constitution" was an expression of his intent "not to seek a consecutive term." The opposition party criticized the statement as "evasive" and "irrelevant," demanding a clear and direct statement from President Lee. Sung Ki-hong, senior presidential secretary for public communication, appeared on an MBC radio program on the 10th and answered "yes" when the host asked, "Can we understand the president's remarks yesterday as meaning he will not seek a consecutive term?" Secretary Sung stated, "Given that the term is already limited within the constitutional order, we interpret it as a statement that a consecutive term itself, as discussed in rumors, is entirely out of the question and cannot even be considered."

Previously, President Lee said during a meeting with overseas Koreans in Paris, France, on the 9th (local time), "Because my term is clearly limited by the Constitution, we must start (summit diplomacy) quickly to reap its effects." It was the first time President Lee directly mentioned the controversial issue of a constitutional amendment allowing consecutive terms in a public setting. Earlier, Senior Presidential Secretary for Political Affairs Hong Ik-pyo addressed the controversy on the 8th, saying, "When President Lee has the opportunity to speak directly, he will make his intentions clearer."

People Power Party leader Jang Dong-hyeok said at a Supreme Council meeting held at the National Assembly that day, "How long do we have to listen to the president's evasive talk?" He added, "If we connect it to constitutional amendment, it is as if he cut off the latter part—'so to do it one more time, a crafty constitutional amendment is absolutely necessary'—and only spoke the first part." People Power Party Floor Leader Chung Jeom-sik also wrote on Facebook, "The fact that the president's term is clearly limited under the current Constitution is something even a child knows," adding, "We are asking him to promise not to change that, but he keeps giving irrelevant answers." He stated, "It is a play on words that is no different from his existing stance," and added, "We fully understand his true intention that he will never say 'I will not seek a consecutive term' or 'I will stand trial,' so do not mock the public with wordplay."

articles.title: [Analysis] Yong Hye-in and Basic Income Party Accused of Misusing Donations Pocketed 2.3 Billion Won in 'Public Money' Over Six Years
articles.summary:
Annual payouts break down as follows: 88,596,540 won for 2020 (seven-month portion); 152,807,360 won for each of 2021 and 2022; 154,263,460 won for 2023; 156,900,820 won for each of 2024 and 2025; and 112,544,110 won for 2026 (eight-month portion). Political funds collected by candidate Yong's sponsorship association from 2020 through 2025 total 758,107,962 won. The amounts were around 63.7 million won in 2020 and about 74.71 million won in 2021, but starting in 2022, approximately 150 million won in donations has been consistently raised each year.

These funds are separate political funds in accounting terms, raised by the sponsorship association and managed to be used exclusively for political activity purposes. State subsidies and election subsidies paid to the Basic Income Party to date total 594,427,920 won. After receiving 15,771,370 won as a regular subsidy in the third and fourth quarters of 2020, the founding period, the party received 32,068,810 won in 2021; 106,632,990 won in 2022 (combined presidential and local election subsidies); 34,981,490 won in 2023; 32,842,350 won in 2024; and 36,319,020 won in 2025.

In the June 3 local elections, the Basic Income Party garnered 0.99% of the vote and, holding one seat in the National Assembly, met the fixed-allocation requirements under the Political Funds Act. As a result, in the third quarter of 2026 alone, it received 277,098,720 won in regular subsidies, a 28-fold increase compared to the second quarter (approximately 9.85 million won). Combined with the local election subsidies, a total of 335.82 million won has reverted to the party this year so far.

Funds flowing from candidate Yong's side into the party have also been confirmed. According to political fund income and expenditure details submitted to the National Election Commission for 2020–2024, lawmaker Yong used a total of 503,959,785 million won in political funds during that period, of which 58.3%, or 293.6 million won, was spent as special party dues. This is the amount transferred to the party from political funds sourced from donations and other revenues.

Recently, suspicions of violations of the Political Funds Act were raised regarding these special party dues expenditure details and the spouse's salary paid by the party, leading to a criminal complaint.

Combining the amounts of the three categories excluding the special party dues yields 2,327,341,712 won. Each fund moved through separated accounting networks categorized into personal salaries (direct National Assembly payments), sponsorship association accounting (donations), and party-attributed funds (state subsidies).

Candidate Yong held a press conference at the National Assembly Communication Hall that day, stating, "The Basic Income Party has run the party well for six years with quarterly state subsidies of 9 million won—an amount that doesn't even cover the labor cost of a single person—and has grown into a small but strong party." She added, "Between the People Power Party, which relies on state subsidies for 35.7% of its total annual revenue, and the Basic Income Party, which has been self-reliant through members' party dues with only 1.6% subsidized by state funds, exactly who is the parasitic party?"

articles.title: "GPU Financing Underway for 3 to 4 Korean Companies," Says Law Firm
articles.summary:
As the artificial intelligence (AI) industry experiences rapid growth, "GPU financing"—a method for efficiently procuring graphics processing units (GPUs), which are core infrastructure assets—has emerged as a major topic in global legal and financial markets. The Law Times conducted a video interview on September 2, 2026, with Don Stokes and Rhys McWhirter, partner attorneys at the global law firm Latham & Watkins who specialize in GPU financing advisory.

Rhys McWhirter stated, "In the United States, multi-billion-dollar GPU financing structures were established a year to a year and a half ago. This is the concept of 'GPUaaS (GPU as a Service),' where massive GPU assets are utilized as a service rather than being taken on the balance sheet as capital expenditures (CapEx). On the other hand, this market in Asia began growing rapidly about six months ago. It is progressing primarily in regions with high national credit ratings that are pursuing Sovereign AI policies, such as South Korea, Singapore, and Japan, while Malaysia and Indonesia are also showing interest."

Don Stokes noted, "Structuring work for three to four large-scale deals related to South Korea is currently underway. These are all companies aiming to secure AI leadership. However, due to bottlenecks in the global GPU supply chain, it takes a lead time of about one year to actually procure the chips. For this reason, there are no final deals fully completed with financial procurement yet, but South Korean conglomerates are participating in the market very actively."

They further explained that law firms intricately refine a series of complex legal relationships, ranging from designing funding structures, off-taker agreements, and IT hardware procurement to credit structuring that connects future computing revenues to loan repayment sources.

Don Stokes explained, "South Korean conglomerates do not participate as borrowers taking out direct loans, but as 'off-takers' (final demandateurs, GPU Customers or Lessees) who purchase the established computing capacity. The borrowers are specialized neocloud companies such as CoreWeave or nScale, which hold Nvidia Cloud Partner (NCP) status. South Korean companies play the role of core customers who practically utilize computing power, much like the Mag 8 hyperscalers do in the U.S. market."

This means that South Korean conglomerates participate as "prime tenants" without incurring trillions of won in debt. The role of the "landlord (borrower)"—who takes out loans to directly purchase and build GPU servers—is assumed by specialized cloud companies like CoreWeave, while domestic conglomerates like Naver take on the role of "core tenants (off-takers)" who pay service fees and utilize GPU computing power. This implies that domestic companies can stably secure cutting-edge AI computing resources like U.S. Big Tech companies while avoiding the risk of placing massive liabilities on their balance sheets.

In addition, because specialized clouds like CoreWeave (the borrower) are key partners (NCPs) prioritized for Nvidia chips, leasing their infrastructure is also a realistic shortcut to securing the latest GPUs most quickly.

Don Stokes stated, "Initial senior loans are led by U.S. private equity firms (such as Apollo and Blue Owl) and global investment banks (such as Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and JPMorgan) that have extensive experience in loan structuring and risk management. However, South Korean financial institutions can also participate by purchasing loan claims in the secondary market. We are holding discussions with several South Korean financial institutions."

Global law firms are holding meetings and briefings regarding this matter. An official at a domestic law firm explained the outlook that the strategic advice of those who have successfully closed deals in the global market will be helpful to South Korean companies.

Rhys McWhirter concluded, "In the Asian market, the 'reseller model' is emerging as an alternative. This is a structure where a conglomerate, acting as the primary off-taker, signs a long-term contract for large-scale GPU capacity and then resells it to domestic small and medium-sized startups or AI-native enterprises under short-term contracts of 12 to 24 months. Conglomerates can earn margins while startups gain access to advanced AI computing assets without heavy capital burdens."

articles.title: The Scandal unleashes forbidden passion in reimagined Joseon
articles.summary:
Netflix's The Scandal reimagines the 1782 novel Dangerous Liaisons in the late Joseon era, centering on Lady Cho, Cho Won and Hui-yeon. Director Jung Ji-woo says he wanted to show Joseon elegance while exploring the unseen dynamic between Lady Cho and Hui-yeon. Starring Son Ye-jin, Ji Chang-wook and Nana, the 19-plus series premieres Sept. 18.

- Jung Ji-woo directed the series and said he wanted to capture the sophistication of the late Joseon era on screen. - The production used hanbok designed by Kim Young-jin of the Tchai Kim Youngjin brand, with distinct color palettes for each lead. - Son said Lady Cho's signature color is light green and that her costumes become darker as the character's ambition deepens. High-society secrets and forbidden passion collide in "The Scandal," Netflix's bold Joseon-era reimagining of the classic 1782 novel "Dangerous Liaisons." Helmed by acclaimed director Jung Ji-woo, best known for films "Happy End" (1999) and "Eungyo" (2012), the series follows Lady Cho (Son Ye-jin) - a mastermind too extraordinary for the era's rigid social boundaries - as she orchestrates a perilous wager with the ultimate playboy, Cho Won (Ji Chang-wook).

When an innocent woman, Hui-yeon (Nana), becomes the target of their bet, a dangerous web of intrigue, rebellion and uncontrollable desire threatens to shatter society's strictest taboos. "The late Joseon era was far more sophisticated and nuanced than we usually imagine," Jung explained during a press conference at JW Marriott Dongdaemun Square Seoul in Seoul, Wednesday. "I wanted to capture that elegance on screen while exploring the complex, unseen dynamic between Lady Cho and Hui-yeon - a relationship never portrayed quite like this before." The novel was previously brought to life in the hit 2003 film "Untold Scandal," a drama starring Lee Mi-sook, Bae Yong-joon, and Jeon Do-yeon, set in the latter part of the Joseon period. articles.title: Park Joon-myeon denies using Mounjaro for weight loss, pleads for belief on 'Natchagim'
articles.summary: Comedian Shin Giru recently brought up Park Joon-myeon's noticeably slimmer appearance, saying, "After my sister appeared on my channel, there was a commotion saying, 'She is so small.' Everyone looks small when they stand next to me anyway." Park drew attention last month when she appeared visibly thinner than before on Shin's YouTube channel "Mwodeun Hagiru." Shin mentioned, "Didn't you go on 'House of Peace'? The video hasn't been uploaded yet, but a writer for that program said you lost too much weight. Rumors started circulating that you were taking Mounjaro." In response, Park expressed frustration, explaining, "There were even articles asking if I took Mounjaro because of that. I didn't use Mounjaro. It's true. Please believe me." Regarding the background of her weight loss, she added, "I accidentally lost weight last year. I lost weight because it was physically demanding while doing performances. If I say this, another article will come out. Please edit this out." Shin also revealed the reason why she does not use Mounjaro either. She shared, "I get a lot of comments asking, 'Why aren't you using Mounjaro?' If I did that, I feel like life would lose its joy. My only way to relieve stress is thinking about 'what to eat after we finish,' and that cannot disappear from my life." articles.title: Ki Eun-se Shares Outdoor Home Dining at Her Pyeongchang-dong Mansion
articles.summary: Actor Ki Eun-se has shared glimpses of her daily life, showcasing her newly moved-in Pyeongchang-dong home. In the newly released photos, Ki is seen wearing an ivory knit cardigan featuring red floral embroidery, paired with gold-rimmed glasses and pearl earrings as she looks into the camera. With one hand gently resting on her chin, she creates a calm and composed atmosphere. In a subsequent selfie, with her hair tied back, she adjusts her bangs with one hand, highlighting her sharp eyes and clean profile. The cozy space, illuminated by soft lighting, naturally conveys an unpretentious, everyday mood. Another photo shows her wearing the same cardigan paired with jeans, standing in front of a dining table on an outdoor terrace. The table, covered with a striped tablecloth, is neatly set with a pot on a portable burner, multiple rice bowls, and various side dishes and vegetables, while Ki focuses on preparing the meal, holding tongs as she checks the pot. A large fringe-decorated parasol combined with the forest scenery in the background further enhances the relaxed weekend vibe. Fans responded enthusiastically with comments such as, "You are so beautiful," "The glasses are so cute," "So pretty," "Fighting," "So pretty," and "I want to live like this too." Previously, Ki moved into her Pyeongchang-dong home in June. The house had previously been embroiled in a nuisance construction controversy during its remodeling. Last May, a netizen on an online community, introducing themselves as a family member of a Pyeongchang-dong resident, claimed that they were experiencing inconveniences such as blocked vehicle traffic and waste issues due to the construction at Ki's home, which amplified the controversy. In response, Ki's agency explained, "We recognized that complaints regarding parking inconveniences and cleaning had arisen, so we apologized directly to the residents and completed cleaning the neighborhood." Following the controversy, Ki also bowed her head in apology while posting photo verification of herself cleaning around the construction area.

articles.title: Kim Keon-hee Tears Up in Final Appeal: 'I Was Bedridden and Not in a Position to Hold Power' - Weekly Kyunghyang
articles.summary: Kim Keon-hee, sentenced to seven years in prison in her first trial on charges of receiving valuables under the guise of job recommendations—often referred to as "office-selling"—tearfully stated during her final appeal hearing on Dec. 9, "I apologize for causing concern to many people due to my shortcomings, and I will live the rest of my life in remorse." Kim made the remarks during the sentencing hearing for charges including aggravated bribery-mediation held before Panel 15-3 of the Seoul High Court (Presiding Judge Sung Eon-joo). "I ask that my entire life not be mischaracterized and that my minimum dignity be preserved," she said. Kim wept throughout her final statement. "I should have been more cautious and resolute," she said, adding, "While I humbly accept the reprimands, I cannot admit to things I did not do." She continued, "I have never received anything in exchange for public office or national projects, and I have never once used presidential authority to grant positions or business opportunities." She went on to say, "I was very sick and confined to bed." "False instigations circulated claiming I held power, but I was in no condition to do so," she added. She also stated, "If I had continued my business and worked hard on exhibitions before marriage, it would have been far more economically beneficial, but because my husband became president, I lost everything." In its closing argument, the special counsel team stated, "Kim was in a position as the president's spouse to directly approach the president and influence public decision-making." They added, "That accessibility and influence were the primary motives for the providers of the valuables." The team further noted, "Although the crime of mediation of influence was applied because she is not a public official, her public influence was tied to private valuables, making the nature similar to that of bribery." The special counsel team requested the court, "The lower court's sentence of seven years is not excessive, so we ask that you dismiss Kim's appeal." Kim is accused of receiving 13.8 million won worth of valuables, including a Van Cleef & Arpels necklace and Graff earrings, from Lee Bong-kwan, chairman of Seohee Construction, in March 2022, along with a request concerning the appointment of his eldest son-in-law, former Prime Minister's Chief of Staff Park Sung-geun. She is also accused of receiving a gold turtle and a replica of Sehando valued at 2.65 million won in April of that year from former National Education Commission Chairperson Lee Bae-yong under the guise of an appointment favor. Furthermore, she faces charges of receiving a Vacheron Constantin wristwatch worth 39.9 million won in September of the same year from DroneDom CEO Seo Sung-bin in exchange for business favors. Around June of that year, she is also accused of receiving Chanel perfume, cosmetics, liquor, and a Dior bag from Pastor Choi Jae-young in exchange for favors related to presidential duties.

articles.title: "Swings Is Stimulating and Scary"... Behind the Scenes of 'Tazza 4'
articles.summary:
A press preview for the film "Tazza: Beelzebub's Song" (directed by Choi Kook-hee, hereinafter "Tazza 4") was held on the 9th at CGV Yongsan I'Park Mall on Hangang-daero in Yongsan-gu, Seoul. Director Choi Kook-hee and actors Byun Yo-han and Noh Jae-won attended the event. "Tazza 4," the final installment of the "Tazza" series, is a crime film about Jang Tae-young (played by Byun Yo-han), who thought he had the world in his hands through an online casino business, and his best friend of the same name, Park Tae-young (played by Noh Jae-won), who stripped him of everything, as they reunite in a global gambling ring for a final showdown of revenge.

Amid this, Moon Ji-hoon drew attention by being cast in the role of the hitman Abraham. Moon Ji-hoon, who has been active as rapper Swings, makes his screen debut through this film. Director Choi said, "Cho Joong-hwan and Abraham do not have a large amount of screen time, but they leave an impact. We held many auditions for Abraham, but we were unable to find a suitable actor." He recalled, "Coincidentally, actor Yo-han showed me a video of actor Ji-hoon performing a free-form acting piece," adding, "I needed a fresh face, and I thought it was fresh."

Noh Jae-won, who acted alongside Moon Ji-hoon, said, "As a person rather than a rapper, I was a fan. There was a lot to learn from his way of life. I thought it took ordinary courage." He continued, "I first saw his acting videos on Instagram and YouTube, and perhaps because I was preparing for Park Tae-young at the time, I even felt jealous of that courage." In response, Byun Yo-han playfully scolded him, saying, "No. Hurry up and get out of [your character]," eliciting laughter.

Despite this, Noh Jae-won continued speaking. He praised him, saying, "I think that video was precious. I don't have that kind of courage. I dare say he would do even better." He then brought laughter by saying, "On set, he was a truly stimulating actor."

Byun Yo-han, who had recommended Moon Ji-hoon, smiled and said, "He has been at the top of a certain stage for 20 years, and when he posted a video stating he wanted to act, I wanted to accept that challenge." He added, "That courage and passion happened to pop up on my algorithm, and I didn't want to turn away from it; I wanted to face it. I actively appealed to the director. By accommodating many opinions, Moon Ji-hoon ultimately ended up playing the role of Abraham." He recalled, "He did his absolute best on set, and tried to do even more."

Byun Yo-han also showered Moon Ji-hoon with praise. He said, "A friend who is good at one thing seems to be good at everything. I think he has become a friend I can respect and admire even more." At the same time, he provoked laughter by adding, "When we were shooting the action scenes, I was genuinely scared."

articles.title: South Korea Moves to Establish Low-Carbon Standards for K-Pop Concerts
articles.summary: Efforts to establish common standards for reducing carbon emissions at K-pop concerts are gaining momentum. The initiative involves management agencies, concert venues, production companies, ticketing platforms, and energy, transportation, and waste management entities working together to measure carbon emissions across the entire concert lifecycle and develop reduction strategies. On December 8, the inaugural policy debate for the "Consultative Body for Establishing Carbon-Neutral Concert and Event Guidelines," hosted by the office of Representative Lee Jung-moon of the Democratic Party of Korea and the K-pop climate action platform Kpop4Planet, was held at the Members' Office Building of the National Assembly in Yeouido, Seoul. Government and public institutions, concert planning and production companies, venue operators, private associations, and experts attended to discuss measures for measuring and managing concert carbon emissions. The consultative body plans to hold a total of five meetings through February next year. This consultative body is significant because it connects eco-friendly efforts previously conducted by individual agencies, concerts, or festivals into industry-wide common standards. Concerts involve multiple stakeholders, from management agencies to venues, production companies, stage installation firms, ticketing platforms, transportation providers, energy suppliers, waste management companies, and audiences. Without consistent methods to measure where and how much carbon is emitted at each stage, it is difficult to set reduction targets. The consultative body plans to first accumulate measurable data, discuss reduction measures and support policies by sector—such as energy, mobility, and waste—and then translate these into guidelines. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism (MCST) has also begun securing baseline data. Kim Yu-mi, head of the Popular Culture Industry Division at the MCST, said, "Assessing the current situation must come first to create guidelines," adding, "We plan to pilot a carbon emission calculator for the concert and event sector to secure data, identify applicable areas and reduction levels, and review the guidelines with the industry next year." The Korea Creative Content Agency (KOCCA) is conducting a beta test of the carbon emission calculator centered around HYBE, SM, and JYP, as well as concert venues in the Seoul and Incheon regions. KOCCA began research on carbon neutrality across the content industry in 2023 and developed a carbon emission calculator for the concert and event sector last year. This year, it is also conducting research on calculating carbon emissions during the production process of music tracks and physical albums. In the field, cost and infrastructure issues were cited as major challenges. Han Moon-gyu, CEO of Sound Alliance, which hosted the eco-friendly festival "Sustainable Wave Festival" at the Incheon Munhak Stadium last August, stated, "Continuous measurement is necessary so that concert producers can understand what can be reduced," and emphasized the need for an intermediary communicator to bridge corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) departments with actual production sites. Cost burdens are also a practical issue. Lee Seo-yoon, CEO of concert planning firm AOD, noted that eco-friendly banners are about three times more expensive than regular printed materials, making government support crucial. Han also stated that the costs associated with the eco-friendly transition should not be concentrated as an additional burden on production companies or organizers. Concerns were also raised that the guidelines could function as de facto regulations. Choi Tae-young, secretary-general of the Korea Music Label Industry Association, suggested that since the scale and conditions of each concert differ, uniform application could be inefficient, proposing that standards be established centered around venues and facilities. Lee Kang-hoon, head of the Future Policy Team at KOCCA, said, "Considering that there are situations where uniform application is realistically difficult, we will draft them carefully so that the industry is not stifled."

articles.title: Figure Skater Cha Jun-hwan to Star in Roy Kim's 'Sparkle' Music Video Ahead of Acting Return
articles.summary: The teaser for Roy Kim's "Sparkle" music video features figure skater Cha Jun-hwan and Seo Soo-min having a chance encounter in a bookstore. The two play a young man and woman who gradually grow closer by passing notes between books. Cha is gearing up for his official acting debut. After starting his career as a child actor, he gained fame as a figure skater before being cast as the lead in the upcoming tvN sitcom "Gungjeon Land." Marking his return to acting after a long hiatus, he will showcase his acting skills through the music video first. His co-star, Seo Soo-min, made her name known by playing So Ji-sub's daughter in the SBS drama "Director Kim," which wrapped up its run in July. This marks the first time Cha and Seo are working together in a project. In the teaser, the two express their emotions without dialogue, focusing on their gazes, facial expressions, and gestures. The clip depicts the process of them starting to become aware of each other as Cha leaves a note between books and Seo discovers it. "Sparkle" is a signature song by the Japanese band RADWIMPS, well known as the soundtrack for the animated film "Your Name." For this remake, lyricist Lee Seu-ran and Roy Kim participated in writing the Korean lyrics. As the fourth release in Roy Kim's "J-POP REMAKE" project, "Sparkle" will be released on various music streaming sites at 6 p.m. on the 11th. The full music video starring Cha Jun-hwan and Seo Soo-min will also be unveiled on the same day.

articles.title: Singer Sung Si-kyung’s Outdoor Concert Draws Complaints Over Operations Amid Praise for His Response
articles.summary: Singer Sung Si-kyung held his "2026 Sung Si-kyung with Friends [Now, Today]" concert on May 5 and 6 at the 88 Lawn Garden of Seoul Olympic Park. Launched in 2022 and previously held indoors, the concert was moved outdoors for the first time this year. Following the event, concertgoers shared mixed reviews about the venue’s operations online. One attendee voiced frustration, writing, "Despite the 160,000-won ticket price per person and a 6 p.m. showtime, we had to line up by 11 a.m. and enter at 2 p.m., sweating under the blazing sun." The attendee added, "They even checked bags and confiscated all our chocolate. A single beer costs 8,000 won. Is everyone who went to Sung Si-kyung's concert okay?" After the post spread across online communities, similar reviews followed. Attendees complained that long waits for food resulted from an insufficient number of food trucks for the size of the crowd, and that there was a lack of adequate shade and separate waiting areas to escape the sun. Claims also emerged that food and beverage prices at the venue were high while outside food was restricted. Concertgoers were seen waiting on mats spread across the lawn or blocking the sunlight with personal umbrellas and parasols. Meanwhile, Sung received praise for his on-site response. Concerned that fans who arrived early would be exhausted from the long wait, he took the stage before the main concert. He performed a duet with Kim Kwang-jin, and Kim Jang-hoon also joined for a surprise performance. Footage of Sung singing in front of waiting audience members before the show was shared online, showing him performing his hit songs while wearing a hat reminiscent of a beekeeper. Some concertgoers suggested that the realities of large-scale outdoor events should be taken into consideration, noting that similar issues frequently occur at outdoor shows. As operational complaints persist following the move to an outdoor venue for "Now, Today," neither the organizers nor Sung's agency have released an official statement. articles.title: Vice Justice Minister Says Leak of Prosecution Documents in Han Dong-hoon Case Constitutes a Crime
articles.summary:
Vice Justice Minister Lee Jin-su said on Jan. 9 that an indictment plan report regarding nominee Kim Seung-won, which was made public by independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon, "is highly likely an internal prosecution document that was leaked." Speaking during a parliamentary interpellation session at the National Assembly, Lee added, "Providing investigative materials constitutes a crime, as it falls under the leakage of official secrets and violations of the Personal Information Protection Act." 

Responding to a question by Democratic Party lawmaker Jeon Yong-ki regarding how lawmaker Han managed to make public the Seoul Western District Prosecutors' Office indictment plan document, Lee stated, "Internal reports produced during the prosecution's decision-making process must not be leaked to the outside under any circumstances." Jeon and other leadership members of the Democratic Party have pointed out that Han has been illegally acquiring and distributing prosecution investigative materials, including the indictment plan document concerning nominee Kim.

On Dec. 4, Han wrote on Facebook, "The Western District Prosecutors' Office decided to indict nominee Kim and delivered an indictment plan in a document to the Supreme Prosecutors' Office and the Ministry of Justice," adding, "Who, and why, blocked Kim Seung-won's indictment and the demand for a prison sentence?"

Asked whether there is a possibility that the investigative team leaked the materials, Vice Minister Lee said, "That possibility cannot be ruled out either," noting that "not only current public officials, but also former public officials are subject to punishment for the leakage of secrets."

Regarding who had access to the document, Lee said, "The investigative team in charge of the frontline investigation, their respective office, and the Supreme Prosecutors' Office investigation line directing it are the parties who can view such reports," adding, "If investigative materials or reports were leaked, such grounds are likely to remain as digital data." He further stated, "The investigation personnel and the Supreme Prosecutors' Office reporting line at the time have been identified to a certain extent."

Lawmaker Jeon criticized the situation, saying, "The prosecution must not become a political sponsor that hands over internal investigative materials to a specific politician to extend the political life of a lawmaker with a prosecutor background." Jeon added, "There are even calls that if criminal allegations are confirmed, they should be investigated, and if structural leaks of investigative materials are uncovered, we must get to the bottom of it, even if it requires a special counsel."

articles.title: ChatGPT Cements Role as Business Tool as OpenAI Strengthens South Korea Strategy
articles.summary:
Marking the first anniversary of the launch of its South Korea office, OpenAI is stepping up its push into the domestic enterprise artificial intelligence (AI) market. The company’s strategy is to expand ChatGPT from a simple work assistant into an enterprise productivity platform capable of independently handling research, analysis, development, and automation. Additionally, domestic weekly active users for ChatGPT Work and Codex—which leverage AI to perform tasks using applications and files—grew about 14-fold over the six months starting in March. Codex is a coding agent that supports writing, editing, and reviewing code, while ChatGPT Work applies Codex's agent technology to ChatGPT to handle everything from research and analysis to document creation. 

OpenAI Korea General Manager Kim noted that the scope and depth of AI utilization among domestic companies have expanded simultaneously. AI has begun to be used across diverse job functions—including legal, sales, finance, marketing, and operations—while the roles assigned to AI within a single workflow have broadened to encompass research, deliverables generation, software development, and task automation. Kim emphasized that organizations such as Samsung Electronics and Seoul National University are establishing foundations for AI use across entire organizations. This signifies that AI has moved beyond specific job roles or small-scale proof-of-concept projects to become a common working environment shared by all members of an organization.

Kim also stressed the expansion of the partner ecosystem to support the deployment and operation of AI in domestic enterprises. Major system integration (SI) firms, cloud and IT operations specialists, and AI startups will join the "OpenAI Partner Network" to help companies adopt AI and spread its use internally. Furthermore, OpenAI plans to expand the supply of its models through platforms such as Amazon Bedrock, diversifying access channels so that companies can choose OpenAI models while maintaining their existing cloud and technology environments.

Kim also introduced strategies for strengthening domestic data processing. Currently, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Edu, and API customers can utilize data residency to store customer content in South Korea. In the cybersecurity sector, he announced the creation of dedicated partners to expand the "Daybreak" service. OpenAI plans to select five or more domestic partners to help companies discover, verify, and respond to security vulnerabilities using AI.

Since June 19, OpenAI has been serving ads to adults using free and paid tiers of ChatGPT in South Korea. The ChatGPT advertising business reached an annualized run rate of $1 billion in revenue in under 200 days since launch and is currently used by tens of thousands of advertisers. A dedicated advertising team has recently been deployed in Korea to expand support for domestic advertisers and agencies, and companies can run ad campaigns directly using a self-service advertising platform.

"The past year has been a time when what South Korean companies expect from AI has become much clearer," Kim said. "The speed and depth of adoption grew together when our services completed actual tasks to the end, connected naturally with existing systems, and operated within the security and control demanded by enterprises."

articles.title: Comedian Lee Hyuk-jae Booked for Drunk Driving After Rear-Ending Motorcycle
articles.summary: Lee Hyuk-jae's blood alcohol concentration measured between 0.03% and 0.08%, a level warranting a license suspension. Police plan to review whether to additionally apply charges of bodily injury resulting from professional negligence under the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents, pending confirmation of the victim's injuries. Lee debuted in 1999 as an open-recruitment comedian for MBC and gained fame through entertainment programs such as "Star Golden Bell." However, he suspended his entertainment activities following a controversy in January 2010 involving an assault on a room salon employee. He has since faced a series of controversies. In 2015 and 2017, he was sued and faced lawsuits for failing to repay debts amounting to hundreds of millions of won. Last year, he failed to pay over 200 million won in national taxes for more than a year, placing him on the National Tax Service's list of high and habitual delinquents.

articles.title: Public-Private Body Formed to Create K-Pop 'Low-Carbon Concert' Guidelines
articles.summary: A public-private-industry-academia consultative body has been launched to establish low-carbon guidelines for the K-pop industry, aiming to induce carbon reduction across the performance sector by setting standards to manage carbon emissions generated during concerts. K-pop4Planet, a climate crisis response platform for K-pop fans, held a launch ceremony and policy debate on the "Consultative Body for Establishing Carbon-Neutral Concert and Event Guidelines" at the National Assembly Member's Office Building in Yeongdeungpo-gu, Seoul, on Dec. 8, discussing carbon-neutral standards and policy directions for the K-pop industry. Concerts are considered the largest source of greenhouse gas emissions in the music industry. Significant carbon is generated not only by energy used for stage lighting, sound, and heating and cooling, but also through the travel of audiences and artists, as well as stage production and waste disposal processes. While the overseas performance industry is increasingly adopting carbon emission measurement and reduction as a new standard for concert operations, South Korea still lacks common calculation standards and operational systems. Lee Ji-eun, a senior researcher at Shin & Kim who delivered a presentation at the event, diagnosed that in the K-pop industry, where overseas tours and international collaborations are active, the capacity to measure and manage carbon emissions can become a competitive edge. As investors and overseas companies heavily evaluate corporate environmental information, she emphasized that carbon neutrality should be approached as a strategy to enhance industrial competitiveness beyond mere regulatory compliance. "The low-carbon transition of K-pop has already begun," Lee said. "To spread the practices of leading companies across the industry, common calculation standards and measurement systems must be established, backed by government and local government support and incentives." In the subsequent discussion, participants voiced the urgent need to secure data for measuring concert carbon emissions and establish common standards. Critics pointed out limitations in calculating emissions due to difficulties in securing information on audience travel, venue energy use, and subcontractor data, as well as differing facilities and management methods across venues. Cho Hyo-jin, CEO of Tomorrow's Use, said, "In the process of measuring carbon emissions from K-pop concerts, we faced difficulties securing data from audiences, venues, and subcontractors," adding, "A data collection system that ticket vendors, concert venues, and subcontractors can use together is needed." Lee Da-yeon, a campaigner for K-pop4Planet, said, "Fans played an absolute role in K-pop growing into music enjoyed by people around the world, and as a fan, I am prouder of this than anyone," adding, "I hope K-pop will set the standard for sustainable performances and show leadership in driving changes in the global music industry."

articles.title: Son Ye-jin, Ji Chang-wook, and Nana Bring Dangerous Desires to Netflix’s 'Scandals'
articles.summary: A press conference for the new Netflix series "Scandals" was held on the 9th at the JW Marriott Dongdaemun Square in Jongno-gu, Seoul. Director Jung Ji-woo and actors Son Ye-jin, Ji Chang-wook, and Nana attended the event to share details about the project. "Scandals" is an eight-part series that depicts a bold and dangerous love wager between Lady Cho (played by Son Ye-jin)—a woman of exceptional talent constrained by the limitations of the Joseon era—and Joseon's ultimate romantic, Cho-won (played by Ji Chang-wook), alongside the story of Hui-yeon (played by Nana), a woman entangled in their bet. Based on French author Pierre Choderlos de Laclos's novel "Dangerous Liaisons" and adapted to the Joseon Dynasty, the series is directed by Jung Ji-woo. It reinterprets the classic's alluring narrative through a 2026 perspective, incorporating Korean sentiment and period settings. The production expands multidimensionally upon the desires of characters who yearn for what their era forbade and attempt to choose their own paths, while adding a modern sensibility. Director Jung explained, "We changed the setting of the 18th-century French novel to Joseon. It is a story where a man and a woman who have built a bond since childhood start a game with lingering feelings between them, and three people—including a new face who gets unexpectedly dragged into it—exchange letters and become swept up in unpredictable emotions and events. I thought of the late Joseon period as a very sophisticated and refined society, and I wanted to portray that era brilliantly." Son Ye-jin, who plays Lady Cho—a woman seeking an autonomous life—revealed that her desire to work with Director Jung and her curiosity about the character led her to join the project. She said with a smile, "I wanted to work with the director. When I was offered the role of Lady Cho, I remembered seeing the film version in the past and became curious about how this story would unfold as a series. The charm of the character Lady Cho herself was also huge. I thought to myself that I am now at an age where I can play this role." She added, "The work deals with human desire, and the fact that it is set in Joseon—where desire was taboo—as well as the fact that it is a historical drama after a long time, were reasons I took on the project." Ji Chang-wook remarked, "The emotions and relationships of the characters in the classic novel 'Dangerous Liaisons' were extremely interesting. The fact that this is being reinterpreted and made into a series in 2026 was also intriguing. I was looking forward to working with the director, and also to joining forces with Ye-jin sunbaenim and Nana. Working with two actresses of such distinct colors in itself was a very fun experience." Nana placed her trust in Director Jung above all else. She stated, "I have long been a fan and admirer of the director. I also felt that if I applied myself to this character, I could express her well. It was an honor to be able to work alongside the senior actors. With various expectations running high, I chose to join the project." Director Jung similarly expressed strong trust in the three actors. Regarding the casting, he emphasized, "Rather than me choosing them, I feel I was chosen. My first priority was wanting to work with Son Ye-jin on Lady Cho. I felt every time that her ability to carry the story on her shoulders and take responsibility for the entire drama is like that of a superhero. That is why I desperately wanted to tackle this difficult role with her." Praising Ji Chang-wook, he noted, "Cho-won had to be an affectionate man. It was wonderful when Ji Chang-wook played affectionate characters in his previous works, and I am deeply grateful to him for adding humor to it as well." As for Nana, he commended her, saying, "I wanted Hui-yeon to step away from the so-called traditional image of a woman, and I thought she was a great fit for actor Nana. While working with her, I was in awe of the strength she possesses." He also showed affection for Han Sun-hwa. Director Jung hinted, "Being here with the three of them feels like coming to a feast, but it feels like I left one actor behind. Han Sun-hwa portrayed a brazen character focused on money and fame with such loveliness, and I definitely wanted to introduce her." Lady Cho, played by Son Ye-jin, is a character harboring desires and talents forbidden by her era. Son Ye-jin explained, "Lady Cho was a woman named Cho-yoon who was independent and autonomous from a young age. She excelled in writing and painting, but in the Joseon era, the places where women could showcase their talents were limited. Ultimately, she compromised with reality and lived as Lady Cho, a noblewoman of the gentry. She is a figure who experienced decisive moments and frustration in her relationship with Cho-won, which shaped her into the Lady Cho she is now."
